game.summary: Duels at sea inside the match room. Protocol v5: Buttons.Grapple (J, latched like E), duel-ready message, 'cancelled' end reason. New apps/server/src/duelMachine.ts (DuelMachine: seats and gates, countdown with probes and input delay, DuelAuthority bundles, reconnection bookkeeping, forfeits at frame boundaries) now runs both DuelRoom (start on countdown; behaviour, messages and tests unchanged) and MatchRoom (start when the rules say so; a countdown that ends early waits in 'waiting' without probes). MatchRoom builds each world tick's snapshot for stepEncounters and applies its events: stop ships, open or start or end duels, return and respawn ships. It reports end+settled on the same tick. Views filter the new grapples/markers/status/duels maps. Reserved and respawning ships are hidden; a fighter who drops keeps the seat for 10 s. Simulation: GRAPPLE_BUTTON, stopShip, returnShip, pointInSight. Web: DuelClient over a DuelTransport seam (duelRoomTransport, SeaDuelRouter); one Phaser game per page (MatchGame: sea + arena scenes); telegraphs, incoming-grapple warning, duel markers with elapsed time, protection ring; HUD lines for grapple/cooldown, warning, protection and respawn. Test tools: HeadlessDuelClient runs over either room; HeadlessClient.fighter. Tests: web/simulation/server/protocol unit tests; integration seaDuel.test.ts (15 concurrent: grapple, escape by range and by aim, no target, protected target, KO, watcher/stranger visibility incl. raw frames, return and respawn, drop/reconnect, 10 s forfeit, quit, both absent, ready forfeit/cancel/late ready) and seaDuelHarness.test.ts (80/20/1%: 181/181 hash checks, 0 desyncs; draw return); e2e seaDuel.spec.ts [scenario:sea-duel]. Harness scripts moved to tests/integration/harness.ts. Docs: architecture.md, duel.md, encounters.md, README. Checks run here: npm ci; npm run typecheck (pass); npm run test:unit (855 pass); npm run test:integration (55 pass, 200 s); npm run build (pass, smoke passed); playwright all 4 spec files with the JSON reporter (7/7 pass), and check-report said the report follows the verifier's rules.
open_assumptions: No player starts with §2 departure protection: private matches have no start of play yet, so createEncounterState gets no spawnProtected ids.

With no rubbings yet, the room sends the end and the settled report on the same world tick (decisions.md). A settled duel's lobby stays in the fighters' views for 2 s (DUEL_RESULT_TICKS) so both can read the result. The winner's protection and the loser's respawn count during it.

Fighters and players waiting to respawn see no other ship, telegraph or marker. A grapple telegraph names its target's id to observers who see the attacker. Duel markers use an opaque key and carry no player ids.
The match page's single Phaser game stays Phaser.AUTO (WebGL where available) with the arena scene inside it. The standalone duel page keeps its canvas-renderer arena game.
A sea duel's HUD 'Duel code' field shows the match code. The dev-only ?rtt=&jitter= latency setting still applies only to standalone duel rooms.

findings.message: Hidden information: a grapple telegraph (GrappleSchema, apps/server/src/MatchRoom.ts updateViews/mirrorEncounters) goes into the view of anyone who sees the attacker, and it always carries defenderId (the target's session id). Grapple range is 6 tiles and sight radius is 10, so an observer who sees the attacker at the edge of sight learns the id, and from the aim and range the rough position, of a target outside its own sight radius. Observers only need the attacker and the aim to draw the telegraph. Blank defenderId for viewers who are neither the target nor able to see it. The worker recorded this as an open assumption, not a requirement.
findings.requirement: a client receives another player's attempt telegraphs, duel markers and ships only within its sight radius, through the existing `StateView` path.

findings.message: 'They stop' is not tested at room level. Every integration grapple that lands (seaDuel.test.ts first test, pairInRange/playersAt) places both ships at rest, so speed 0 and an unchanged position during the reservation would hold even if MatchRoom never stopped a moving ship. Only the pure stopShip helper is tested on a moving ship (simulation.test.ts). The e2e host coasts into the grapple but nothing asserts that its ship stops.
findings.requirement: a hit reserves both ships (they stop and ignore sailing input)

The forfeit case checks >= 9.5 s since the grapple. A cancel at the countdown's end instead of 10 s would still pass.

inputs.feature: Pirate Sea Race encounters online (duels at sea)
inputs.decisions:
# Decisions: encounters-online

From the overnight session of 2026-09-24/25. The operator is asleep and asked the assistant to decide, record each decision, and use the workflow for the code.

## Decisions

- Slice 4's second half. The pure rules (`encounters-core`) are on `main`. This feature wires them into `MatchRoom` together with the online duel. Theft and rubbings follow in `rubbings-theft`, so this feature stays a size one lane can finish, and fighting at sea can be played on its own first.
- The duel runs inside `MatchRoom` as a simulation object (§14): one `DuelAuthority` per duel, fed by the same netcode as the standalone duel. The standalone `DuelRoom` stays as the practice arena and for private 1v1s, and keeps its tests.
- One server class holds the duel machine (countdown, probes and input delay, forfeits, bundles, reconnection). `DuelRoom` and `MatchRoom` both use it, so the two can't drift (the lesson of `DuelInputGate`).
- The web duel client gets a transport seam, so one client works over either room.
- One Phaser game per page, with sea and arena scenes, so a duel never leaks a second game.
- J is the grapple, as in §8. It is latched like E, so a tap counts.
- Duel markers follow the same sight rule as ships (§16). Only fighters receive duel traffic.
- Absence in a duel is handled as in the standalone duel: neutral after 250 ms, forfeit after 10 s, a quit forfeits at once. Outside a duel, leaving still removes the ship; the 60 s seat reservation comes with `rubbings-theft`.
- The browser check's timeout rises to 1,200 s for the added `sea-duel` scenario.

## Assumptions

- Encounter tuning stays as `encounters-core` set it (6-tile grapple, ±22.5° hit area, 6 s miss cooldown) until a playtest.
- With no rubbings yet, a duel's settlement happens at the fight's end.

## Deferred

- Theft, gold, the theft-choice UI, collecting rubbings, and the world seat reservation: `rubbings-theft`.
- Fruit kits in duels (pedestals, eating, the arena drawing): `fruit-kits-online`.
- Walking on islands and the island challenge: `objectives-endgame`.

concerns.message: Two clocks own the transition. The encounter rules already decide the countdown, readiness, the 10 s unready forfeit and the both-unready cancel (stepEncounters step 4: duel-started / duel-forfeited / duel-cancelled, in 20 Hz ticks). DuelRoom's machine has its own 180-frame countdown and starts fighting at 0 with no readiness check (DuelRoom.ts:259-268). The plan extracts 'countdown' into the shared class but never says who decides the start and the end inside MatchRoom. Recommend: in MatchRoom the rules are the only authority on phase. duel-reserved starts the machine's probing countdown, with the delay chosen at countdown-30 as today. duel-started steps the authority. duel-forfeited or duel-cancelled finishes the duel. The machine's own quit, absence and KO results go to the rules only as an `end` report, followed by `settled` on the same tick (reports sort ends before settlements). The machine starts itself at countdown 0 only in DuelRoom mode.
concerns.consequence: If the machine's countdown runs on its own, the authority steps while an unready client is still loading its arena. Or the rules and the machine each end the same duel: the rules refuse one report with `already-ended`, and the clients see one winner while the sea applies another. DuelRoom's unchanged behaviour (no ready gate) also breaks if the gate is hard-wired into the shared class.

concerns.message: In sea-duel, the 'guest quits' option can't meet the scenario. A quit leaves MatchRoom, and outside a duel leaving removes the ship because the seat reservation is out of scope. So the guest can never see a respawn countdown or its ship at a dock. The 'host wins with held attack keys' option is also misleading: attacks fire on the press edge (`pressed = bits & ~fighter.held`, duel/step.ts:243). A held J lands one jab, and the round then runs to the 60 s timeout. Grapple windup 1 s + countdown 3 s + round 60 s + respawn 15 s comes to more than 80 s, over playwright.config.ts's 60 s per-test timeout.
concerns.consequence: A worker who picks quit gets stuck on an unprovable assertion. One who holds J hits the 60 s test timeout and either debugs it late or shortens the rules only for tests. Recommend: the host taps J/K in a loop until KO, and set test.setTimeout of about 150 s in that spec.

concerns.message: The integration budget remedy is wrong. vitest.config.ts sets `fileParallelism: false`, so splitting the harness into more files saves no time. The suite already runs 4 harness scenarios of about 14 s each and several 10–15 s reconnection tests. The new tests add these real-time waits: the ready-timeout forfeit (10 s), the both-unready cancel (10 s), the absence forfeit (10 s plus setup), reconnect-and-resume, a scripted KO, the in-match harness (about 12 s), the respawn (15 s) plus the 20 s protection, and the winner's 8 s. A real draw costs a 60 s round plus 10 s overtime.
concerns.consequence: Run serially, the suite likely passes 300 s, and the integration check times out late in the run. Recommend: run independent scenarios concurrently in separate matches in one test (as duel.test.ts:304 already does). Prove the draw return through the cancel path (`settle` treats cancelled like a draw). Assert protection from its endTick instead of waiting it out. Time the suite as soon as the first match-duel tests exist.

concerns.message: Departure protection is undecided. createEncounterState can give every player 45 s of spawn protection (SPAWN_PROTECTION_SECONDS = 45), but MatchRoom has no match-start phase. If the worker grants it at join, following §2, nobody can be grappled for 45 s. The 'protected target can't be grappled' test also needs some way to make a target protected.
concerns.consequence: Every grapple integration test and the sea-duel scenario would wait 45 s, which breaks both time budgets. Or the worker invents an ad hoc bypass. Recommend: no departure protection in private matches until a match-start phase exists. Test the protected target with a winner's 8 s protection, or with a test-placement-style hook.

concerns.message: Adding onDrop and allowReconnection to MatchRoom changes the drop behaviour of every match client. Today a drop goes straight to onLeave, and match.test.ts asserts the player count falls. Reconnection must be granted only to fighters. A reconnected fighter's `client.view` (StateView) must be rebuilt, or its sea view and duel state come back empty. HeadlessClient also has no reconnection path yet.
concerns.consequence: Non-fighters who drop linger as ghosts, and the existing match tests break. Or a fighter who reconnects inside 10 s resumes the duel with no sea view and no duel state, which fails acceptance 4's resume test.

concerns.message: `duelIdFor` embeds both session ids (`duel:tick:len:attacker:defender`). Keep that id out of anything a non-fighter receives: marker map keys, marker fields, and attempt telegraphs to third parties. Key duel-state schemas and ready messages by the duel. Accept a ready only for the recipient's current duel, and only in transition.
concerns.consequence: Keyed by duelId, the marker names its fighters to every client in sight, against duelMarkers' 'nothing names its players' and §16. A stale ready from a previous duel could start a new fight before the arena loads.

challenge.simpler_alternative:
Keep the settled architecture: the duel inside MatchRoom and one shared machine. Make both seams as thin as possible:
(1) The encounter rules drive the machine's phase. The machine exposes beginCountdown / start / finish plus an autoStart flag that only DuelRoom sets, so no second transition policy exists.
(2) Give each duel's per-fighter state the exact field shape of DuelRoomStateSchema (phase, countdown, seed, seats, inputDelay, winner, reason). Put it in a MapSchema on MatchStateSchema under an opaque key and add it only to the two fighters' StateViews. Frames and probes go by client.send to the fighters.
The web DuelClient and HeadlessDuelClient then need only one seam: where the duel-state schema lives, plus send and onMessage. No message-based mirror of the duel state is needed, and hidden information reuses the one mechanism the room already has.
challenge.cheap_experiment:
A 30-minute Colyseus 0.18 spike, run as a throwaway vitest integration test. Build a room with StateView and a MapSchema<DuelSchema>, and add one entry to client A's view only. Then check:
(a) Client B's decoded state never contains the entry, and a raw-message tap on B shows no bytes for it.
(b) Sever A through ImpairmentProxy, call allowReconnection from onDrop, and restore A. Does the reconnected Client keep its `view`, or must onReconnect rebuild it?
(c) Sever B, whose onDrop doesn't call allowReconnection. Does onLeave still fire promptly?
If (a) or (b) fails, the per-fighter duel state must travel as messages instead of a view-filtered schema. That changes the transport seam's design before any worker builds on it.

game.task:
# Task: game

## Goal

Make fights happen at sea. A captain sails within range of a rival, presses J, and after a telegraphed one-second grapple windup the target can still escape. On a hit, both players see a three-second countdown, fight the online duel from the combat spike **inside the match room**, and return to the sea. The winner sails on with escape protection. The loser respawns at a safe dock 15 s later with longer protection. Everyone else sees a duel marker on the sea. This is the first time the two halves of the game meet, so it has to feel good: readable telegraphs, a fair escape, a tense countdown and a clean return.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §6 (all of it), §8 (J grapples in the world), §12 (disconnect in a duel: neutral inputs after 250 ms, forfeit after 10 s absent; both absent), §14 ("Match and duel boundaries": duels are simulation objects inside the match room; fighters receive their arena stream, others only an encounter marker), §15 and §16 (hidden information).
- Read `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/duel.md` and `docs/encounters.md`. Then read the code they map:
  - `packages/simulation/src/encounters`: the pure encounter rules this feature wires in, `stepEncounters` and its events.
  - `packages/simulation/src/netcode`: `DuelAuthority`, `DuelClientSession`, `inputDelayFromSamples`, `linkStats`.
  - `apps/server/src/DuelRoom.ts`: the standalone duel's countdown, probes, input delay, forfeits and practice dummy.
  - `apps/server/src/MatchRoom.ts`, `inputGate.ts`, `duelInputGate.ts` and `schema.ts`.
  - `apps/web`: `main.ts`, `seaScene.ts`, `duelClient.ts`, `arenaScene.ts`, `duelHud.ts`, `keyboard.ts`, `devLatency.ts`.
  - `packages/test-tools` (`HeadlessClient`, `HeadlessDuelClient`, `ImpairmentProxy`) and `tests/integration/duelHarness.test.ts`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`. Playwright's Chromium for `@playwright/test` 1.63.0 is installed and shared read-only; never run `playwright install`.
- The duel simulation now has the Ember and Smoke kits (`docs/fruit-kits.md`); a duel created without kits is the Duelist mirror. Use the duel simulation only through its exports and never change `packages/simulation/src/duel` or `packages/content/src/moves` (not owned). Kits in sea duels come later (`fruit-kits-online`).
- Other features run at the same time in `packages/simulation/src/intel`, `packages/content/src/intel`, `packages/simulation/src/objectives` and `packages/content/src/objectives`. Never touch those paths.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Keep the existing structure, names and patterns. Reuse rather than copy:
  - Extract the standalone duel's machine (countdown, probes and input delay, forfeits, bundles, reconnection bookkeeping) from `DuelRoom` into one server class that both `DuelRoom` and `MatchRoom` use. `DuelRoom`'s behaviour, messages and tests stay the same.

scenarios.description: One browser creates a private match from the landing page; the HUD shows the code, the protocol version, one player and a connected status.
Two browsers join the same private match with their ships in sight of each other; one sails with the keyboard and the other browser's view shows that ship at the new server-authoritative position.
A browser sails its ship around a shoal to an island dock with the keyboard and docks there; the HUD shows the dock and the ship stops at it.
Two browsers in one match with their ships out of sight of each other: neither view lists or draws the other ship until one sails within the sight radius, and it disappears again when it sails away.

One browser opens a practice duel against the dummy, lands a jab and then a keyboard throw (J then K a frame apart); the dummy's health bar and the HUD drop by the move data's damage, and hitboxes can be shown.

Two browsers: one creates a duel, the other joins by its code; after the countdown the first lands a strike on the second, and both views show the same authoritative health, round clock and result, with the connection line showing input delay and corrections.

Two browsers in one match are placed within grapple range; the host sails at the guest and presses J; both see the grapple telegraph, then a three-second countdown and the arena; the duel is decided; the winner returns to the sea with protection shown, and the loser sees a respawn countdown and then their ship at a dock.

completion.summary: Duels at sea inside the match room. Protocol v5: Buttons.Grapple (J, latched like E), duel-ready message, 'cancelled' end reason. New apps/server/src/duelMachine.ts (DuelMachine: seats and gates, countdown with probes and input delay, DuelAuthority bundles, reconnection bookkeeping, forfeits at frame boundaries) now runs both DuelRoom (start on countdown; behaviour, messages and tests unchanged) and MatchRoom (start when the rules say so; a countdown that ends early waits in 'waiting' without probes). MatchRoom builds each world tick's snapshot for stepEncounters and applies its events: stop ships, open or start or end duels, return and respawn ships. It reports end+settled on the same tick. Views filter the new grapples/markers/status/duels maps. Reserved and respawning ships are hidden; a fighter who drops keeps the seat for 10 s. Simulation: GRAPPLE_BUTTON, stopShip, returnShip, pointInSight. Web: DuelClient over a DuelTransport seam (duelRoomTransport, SeaDuelRouter); one Phaser game per page (MatchGame: sea + arena scenes); telegraphs, incoming-grapple warning, duel markers with elapsed time, protection ring; HUD lines for grapple/cooldown, warning, protection and respawn. Test tools: HeadlessDuelClient runs over either room; HeadlessClient.fighter. Tests: web/simulation/server/protocol unit tests; integration seaDuel.test.ts (15 concurrent: grapple, escape by range and by aim, no target, protected target, KO, watcher/stranger visibility incl. raw frames, return and respawn, drop/reconnect, 10 s forfeit, quit, both absent, ready forfeit/cancel/late ready) and seaDuelHarness.test.ts (80/20/1%: 181/181 hash checks, 0 desyncs; draw return); e2e seaDuel.spec.ts [scenario:sea-duel]. Harness scripts moved to tests/integration/harness.ts. Docs: architecture.md, duel.md, encounters.md, README. Checks run here: npm ci; npm run typecheck (pass); npm run test:unit (855 pass); npm run test:integration (55 pass, 200 s); npm run build (pass, smoke passed); playwright all 4 spec files with the JSON reporter (7/7 pass), and check-report said the report follows the verifier's rules.
open_assumptions: No player starts with §2 departure protection: private matches have no start of play yet, so createEncounterState gets no spawnProtected ids.

With no rubbings yet, the room sends the end and the settled report on the same world tick (decisions.md). A settled duel's lobby stays in the fighters' views for 2 s (DUEL_RESULT_TICKS) so both can read the result. The winner's protection and the loser's respawn count during it.

Fighters and players waiting to respawn see no other ship, telegraph or marker. A grapple telegraph names its target's id to observers who see the attacker. Duel markers use an opaque key and carry no player ids.
The match page's single Phaser game stays Phaser.AUTO (WebGL where available) with the arena scene inside it. The standalone duel page keeps its canvas-renderer arena game.
A sea duel's HUD 'Duel code' field shows the match code. The dev-only ?rtt=&jitter= latency setting still applies only to standalone duel rooms.
untested: A browser fighter who drops and reconnects mid-duel at sea (covered only with headless clients through the impairment proxy).
A browser whose arena loads after the 3 s countdown (the 'waiting' pause and session restart are covered only headless).
Arena frame rate and input feel inside the WebGL match game on a GPU-less machine, beyond the sea-duel scenario passing.
More than one simultaneous duel at sea in one match, and the four-duel cap, through the room (covered only by the pure encounter rules' tests).
completion.verify_yourself: Play a sea duel in two real browsers with `npm run dev`: check that the arena inside the match's WebGL game feels as responsive as the standalone canvas arena, and that the one-second telegraph and warning are readable in time to escape.
